newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end firm just off session highs.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end firm just off session highs.

text.p: Italian shares ended just off intraday highs on Wednesday after getting off to a firmer start following the widely expected U.S. Fed funds rate rise on Tuesday last night, with Milan underpinned by foreign markets and the dollar, traders said.

The stock market was also supported by a stronger lira and bond futures on relief that Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi received support from his coalition partners and the far left for his 1997 mini-budget due to be revealed on Thursday.
The blue chip Mib30 index ended up 1.39 percent at 17,697 while the all-share Mibtel index closed 1.29 percent higher at 11,973.

Some caution crept in as Wall Street started lower this afternoon, but most had expected the 0.25 percentage point rise in the Fed Funds rate to 5.5 percent, the first rise for over two years, and saw the weakness in U.S. stocks as temporary.
"The rate rise was the most widely expected event of the year. On the Italian side, the budget confidence has helped light buying interest in stocks," said one dealer.

Telecoms stocks again stood out as the STET extraordinary shareholders meeting aproved a government golden share and set a price for Telecom Italia shareholders who wanted to cash in rather than gain shares in the merged STET-Telecom.
STET gained 0.47 percent to 7,510 lire, Telecom Italia ended up 0.59 percent at 4,290, while mobile phone operator TIM gained 2.97 percent to 4,925.

Shares in financial holding group Gemina were suspended at the 10 percent limit up after the group said late Tuesday it would pay a 1996 ordinary share dividend of 200 lire per share, and 750 lire on its savings shares.
The 10 percent limit was later widened to 15 percent and the shares ended the day up 12.6 percent at 707.6 lire.
